questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.topic: Condition for parallel lines
questions.learningObjective: apply the equal-slope condition for two lines to be parallel
questions.stem: Two hiking routes are written as y equals 4x plus 1 and y equals 4x minus 6. What is the relationship between these two routes?

options.text: They are parallel, since both have slope 4 with different y intercepts
They are perpendicular, since the intercepts differ by the amount of the slope
options.misconception: derives perpendicularity from a gap between intercepts rather than from slopes

options.text: They meet once, since different intercepts always force a single crossing
options.misconception: believes differing intercepts guarantee an intersection point

options.text: They are parallel, since any two rules written with y cannot cross
options.misconception: reads a geometric property off the notation instead of off the slope

questions.explanation: Parallel lines share a slope and differ in their intercepts, and here both slopes are 4 while the intercepts 1 and negative 6 are different, so the two never meet. Perpendicularity would need slopes whose product is negative 1, which two equal slopes cannot supply. The rule to carry over is that the slope decides the direction of a line, and two lines with the same direction either coincide or stay apart for good.
questions.hint: Compare the slopes first, then compare the intercepts to see whether the lines coincide.

questions.topic: Condition for perpendicular lines
questions.learningObjective: find the slope of a line perpendicular to a line of given slope
questions.stem: A cable has slope 5 halves. What must the slope of any cable crossing it at a right angle be?

options.text: Negative 2 fifths, the negative reciprocal of the slope 5 halves
2 fifths, the reciprocal of 5 halves with its sign left unchanged
options.misconception: omits the sign change that perpendicular slopes require

options.text: Negative 5 halves, the given slope with only the sign reversed
options.misconception: reverses the sign without also taking the reciprocal

options.text: 5 halves, the given slope copied over with no transformation at all
options.misconception: copies the slope across and performs no transformation

questions.explanation: Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals of one another, so the slope 5 halves forces the slope negative 2 fifths, and the check is the product: 5 halves times negative 2 fifths is negative 1, which is the signature of a right angle. Taking the reciprocal alone leaves both slopes rising in the same direction, and reversing the sign alone leaves the same steepness, so each partial version fails the product test. The reciprocal of zero is the special case of a vertical line, which is why no horizontal answer can appear here.
questions.hint: The two slopes must multiply to negative 1, so try the negative reciprocal.

options.text: They meet once, since the two equations were written on different days and differ
options.misconception: believes any difference between two equations forces a single crossing

options.text: They are perpendicular, since the left coefficients 3 and 4 give a product of 12
options.misconception: tests perpendicularity with a coefficient product instead of with the slopes

questions.stem: A cable route is mapped by the two points where x is 1 and y is 5, and where x is 7 and y is 21. What is the slope of the route? Report the number only.
questions.explanation: The slope is the rise over the run, so it is 21 minus 5, which is 16, divided by 7 minus 1, which is 6, and 16 over 6 is 2.6 when written as a decimal. Swapping the two changes turns the answer into 6 over 16, which is 0.375 and is the commonest slip.

Zero, because the wall runs up and down while staying in one column
options.misconception: describes the behaviour of a horizontal line and assigns it to a vertical one
